resources.string: Detects the foreground app from window metadata for automatic overlays and allows trusted main-display opacity up to 100%. Optional hardware shortcuts can control overlays. Screen text is not saved or uploaded.
Choose · Adjust · Show. No app binding needed.
Manual priority: Quick Use pauses automatic rules on this display. Stopping it resolves the latest foreground app.
Images stretch to fill the selected display. Quick Use keeps priority over automatic app rules.
Notifications are off. Stop overlays in EasyOverlay or end the session from the system Active apps panel.
Cannot open system settings. Open the app permission settings manually.
Allow display over other apps, then return and start again.
Automatic switching needs a foreground-app detector. Grant Usage Access or enable an enhanced detector, then try again. Quick Use does not need it.
Enable monitoring when you need it
Save an image for an app and enable its rule to switch with the foreground app. Quick Use always takes priority.
Choose an app, import an image, and adjust opacity. You can edit rules while monitoring is off.
The rule will be removed. Its image stays in your library.
Name or package; you can also type a package
Images fill the target display and may be stretched.
After saving, enable automatic monitoring in Settings to switch with the app.
When a detector cannot reliably identify the foreground app on a secondary display, save the rule and choose its image for Quick Use on that display.
Images stay in EasyOverlay private storage. Resolve backup conflicts here. Images still in use cannot be removed.
Your library is empty. Import an image first.
On · Manual overlays always take priority
Off · Use Usage Access or an enhanced detector
The previous automatic session is not running. Check monitoring and background settings, or start it again.
Ordinary overlay permission; Accessibility can provide trusted main-display overlays
Allowed · Stop overlays from the notification
Not allowed · The system may only list the session in Active apps
Uses system dynamic colors and font size settings.
Only changes EasyOverlay. Android remembers your language choice.
Images use private app storage; no folder selection is needed on first launch. Export a backup before uninstalling.
View images, resolve backup conflicts, or choose an image for Quick Use
Includes versioned JSON and original images; excludes permissions and running sessions
Verifies integrity before merging; existing rules take priority
Permissions, running modes, recent switches, and redacted events
Multiple displays, hardware shortcuts, floating control, and display bounds
The system may still limit overlays on secure pages, navigation bars, or external displays
Off by default. Tap to toggle the main display, drag to an edge, or hold to stop everything. The control receives touch input; keep it away from game buttons.
With accessibility enhancements enabled, bind physical keys to control overlays. Screen text is not read. Some devices do not deliver every physical key to apps.
Not allowed · Standard Quick Use still works
Add EasyOverlay from the system Quick Settings editor. Tap to toggle selected Quick Use images. If no image is selected or permission is missing, EasyOverlay opens.
Press up to three physical keys. Combinations cannot overlap existing bindings. Press Back to cancel.
The system restricts background activity for this app. Sessions may stop after you leave. Check system battery settings.
Overlay permission was revoked. Automatic overlays are paused; grant permission again.
Usage Access was revoked. Grant permission again or choose another detector.
The screen is off or locked. Automatic rules are paused.
The system blocked a background start. Return to EasyOverlay to start again.
Monitoring or permissions are restricted. Check system settings and start again.
Show package names on this page
Quick Use takes priority over rules on its display. After process termination, old windows are not reported as still running.
Optional if Accessibility or Shizuku is available
Export and copy always hide target package names and exclude file URIs, user directories, and image paths. Nothing is automatically uploaded.
If sessions keep stopping, check system battery settings and restart from EasyOverlay. Secure pages, the lock screen, permission dialogs, and some external displays may hide overlays.
EasyOverlay is developed independently by Hycnyl.
Libraries: AndroidX / Compose / DataStore (Apache-2.0), Kotlin / kotlinx.coroutines (Apache-2.0), Gson (Apache-2.0), Shizuku API and Dhizuku API (MIT). Image decoding uses Android system components.
Platform behavior and device background restrictions can vary. Diagnostics show the current session state.
Cannot preview this image. Choose it again.
Choose an image to get started
The operation could not finish. Check the image, file access, and available storage, then try again.
The app list is unavailable. You can enter an app package name manually.
Backup imported. Resolve conflicts in the image library.
Bind at most three physical keys
This combination overlaps an existing shortcut. Clear that binding first.
Display %1$d is disconnected. Choose another display.
Verified %1$d images and %2$d rules. Existing rules and Quick Use selections take priority; conflicts remain in the library. Running windows and system permissions are not included.
Found %1$d displays. Secondary displays support independent Quick Use. Automatic switching uses only the main display when the detector cannot reliably distinguish secondary foreground apps.

Android limits touch obscuring for standard overlays. The current maximum is %1$d%%; the slider and actual window use the same value. PNG / GIF transparency is preserved. The floating control receives touches and can be moved to an edge.
Secondary automatic detection depends on the detector. If uncertain, only the main display switches automatically. Manual priority applies independently per display.

Visible overlay and automatic monitoring sessions with stop controls
Automatic monitoring is on · waiting for a matching app
Automatic monitoring paused · open EasyOverlay to check status

Repeated restarts were paused. Open the app to start a fresh session.
Choose a source for detecting the foreground app. Accessibility reacts to window changes; Shizuku reads task snapshots. Usage Access is a fallback. Manual Quick Use keeps priority.
Enable Accessibility, authorize Shizuku, or allow Usage Access, then start monitoring.

Detects foreground apps from window changes and enables trusted main-display overlays up to 100%. Only package/window metadata is used; screen text is not saved or uploaded. Hardware shortcuts are optional.
Try to resume a session you enabled after system reclaim, reboot or update. Explicit stops are respected. Android and device battery rules can still block recovery.
Review battery optimization and device-specific background limits
Optional. Start Shizuku first, then authorize EasyOverlay. Its task reader runs only for monitoring or an explicit operation. It cannot guarantee unlimited lifetime.

For devices already managed by Dhizuku. Device/Profile Owner permission is different from Shizuku shell access and does not provide global task monitoring. Notification permission management is optional.
The device administrator will manage notification permission for EasyOverlay. Review this change before applying; the original policy can be restored.

Uses Shizuku only for EasyOverlay: notifications, Usage Access and the system battery whitelist. Preview changes first; restore the original settings later. Device-specific cleanup rules may still apply.
Allow Usage Access for app switching
Add to the system battery whitelist
This optional service is unavailable or not authorized. Check its connection and permission, then retry.
Settings changed since the preview. Preview again before applying.
Restore the previous optimization before creating a new one.

Opacity above 80% can obscure important screen content and controls. Continue only if you have a reliable way to stop the overlay, such as a configured hardware shortcut. A red slider will remain as a warning.
Do not show this warning again
A connected Accessibility service permits trusted main-display overlays up to 100%. Values above 80% remain red. Other displays use the normal system limit.
Without a connected trusted overlay service, this display uses the Android touch-safety limit. Enable Accessibility for extended main-display opacity.
Extended opacity is unavailable; the actual window is limited to the safe system value.
Waiting for a current foreground observation
Usage Access reconstructs recent activity transitions and may be less accurate in multi-window mode. Prefer Accessibility or Shizuku for faster detection.
EasyOverlay: tap to toggle the main overlay, drag to move, hold to stop all
Session recovery settings could not be saved. Check storage and retry.
Extended trusted opacity is available on the main display only.
The selected source is unavailable. Review permission and connection settings.
Display your images over apps, with quick controls and automatic app rules.
Restore the saved notification permission, Usage Access modes and system battery whitelist for EasyOverlay. Only settings changed by this optimization will be restored.
Restore the saved notification grant and administrator policy for EasyOverlay. Android may close this app when notification permission is revoked. Reopen it to verify and finish the restoration.
A restore point is already saved. Restore it before applying another optimization.
Notification permission may be allowed while app notifications or the session channel remain disabled. Check system notification settings.
The service took too long to start. Refresh the connection and retry.
The privileged query timed out. A fallback is used when available.
The service could not read foreground tasks. Check its status or choose another source.
The system could not safely restore notification permission. Review it in system settings, then retry restoration. The restore point is kept.
